get_groups.description: List the doors and their ports (JMCP GET_GROUPS).

get_transition.description: Read a port's door position and status (HM_GET_TRANSITION). Poll this; the gateway pushes nothing.

port.description: Port id from the groups list.

login.description: Start a session as a gateway user. The reply's token goes in every later packet.
login.example_notes: User 'username', password 'password', tag 3, placeholder gateway MAC.

password.description: That user's password. Sent in clear; see device.notes.

send_impulse.advanced_reason: Moves a motorised door or gate, which can trap or injure. Send only as a deliberate action with the door in view; see device.safety_advisory.
send_impulse.description: Send a port's radio impulse (SET_STATE): the same as pressing that button on a hand transmitter. What the door does depends on the port type and its state. The reply is a Transition.

port.description: Port id from the groups list.

identity.notes: The mac attribute of the discovery reply; GET_MAC (0x02) returns the same six bytes over TCP.

methods.notes: Broadcast the ASCII text <Discover target="Gateway" /> (the probe_hex above) to 255.255.255.255 port 4001; halacs repeats it every 5 s. Each gateway answers with one XML element, e.g. <LogicBox swVersion="2.5.0" hwVersion="1.0.0" mac="54:10:EC:00:00:01" protocol="MCP V3.0"/> (placeholder MAC), from its own address. The reply is XML, which the schema's response_format vocabulary does not name, so it is left unset; read the mac attribute for identity. Gateways on another subnet or behind a VPN are added by address.

device.name: Hörmann BiSecur Gateway
device.notes:
The BiSecur Gateway bridges Hörmann's BiSecur 868 MHz radio (garage and gate operators, entrance doors, receivers) to the home LAN. The BiSecur app talked to it directly on the LAN and through Hörmann's relay when away from home. Hörmann now sells the homee hub as the replacement for both the gateway and the app; a dealer reports the gateway has not been sold since December 2020, users saw an in-app notice in October 2023 announcing the change-over, and community reports from 2025-2026 say the app and the relay are gone. The gateway itself keeps answering on the LAN.
The LAN protocol (the SDKs call it MCP; the discovery reply says "MCP V3.0") is a request/response exchange on TCP 4000. Every frame is sent as upper-case hex ASCII: a 14-byte transport header (source and destination MAC, length), a packet (tag, session token, command id, payload, checksum), and a one-byte transport checksum over the hex text. Log in with a gateway user's name and password to get a session token, then list the doors ("groups" and their "ports"), read a door's position and status, and send it an impulse — the same button press a hand transmitter sends.
SECURITY: the protocol has no encryption. Logins cross the LAN in clear, and SEC Consult's 2020 advisory found the session weak enough to take over from the same network. Keep the gateway on a trusted segment, never expose TCP 4000 beyond it, and give the client its own gateway user rather than the admin account.

openness.notes: Hörmann never published the protocol and declined a request to do so (halacs/BiSecur README). Two independent community SDKs (Python and Go) and a protocol write-up agree on the framing.

safety_advisory.detail: An impulse is a button press: depending on the port type and the door's state it opens, stops, or closes the door, and a closing door or gate can trap or injure a person, pet or vehicle. Hörmann's own guide warns of unintended travel while teaching radio codes. A client must make the impulse a deliberate action, show the door's reported state and position first, and never send it on a schedule or from an automation that runs without someone watching. The gateway's position feedback depends on the operator: ports added by copying a hand transmitter's code report nothing, so the client may not know which way the door will move.
safety_advisory.summary: Sending an impulse moves a heavy motorised door or gate; only send one with the door in view.

security_advisory.detail: SEC Consult's 2020 advisory found that logins cross the LAN in clear and that a session can be hijacked from the same network, which is enough to operate the doors the gateway controls. Keep the gateway on a trusted network segment and never forward TCP 4000 to the internet.
security_advisory.summary: The gateway's LAN protocol has no encryption, and its sessions can be taken over by anyone on the same network.

credentials.notes: Credentials cross the LAN in clear inside the LOGIN frame. Never log or store captured frames without stripping the LOGIN payload.

factory_reset.description: No public source gives a reset procedure for the gateway, and the quick guide has none. Nothing is transcribed here.
factory_reset.effect: Not established. A reset would presumably clear the gateway's users, doors and Wi-Fi settings, which a client cannot set up again without the management commands this spec leaves out.

methods.description: Find the gateway by broadcast or address, open TCP 4000 and log in as a gateway user to get a session token.
methods.name: Connect and log in

steps.action: Connect the gateway to the router by Ethernet, or use the Wi-Fi it was given in the app. The LED is steady green once it is on the network.
Broadcast the discovery probe to UDP 4001, or take the gateway's address from the user.
steps.expect: A LogicBox reply carrying the gateway's MAC and protocol version.

steps.action: Open TCP 4000 and send LOGIN (0x10) with the user name and password, token 0.
steps.expect: A LOGIN reply (0x90) carrying a sender id and a 4-byte session token, or ERROR (0x01) with LOGIN_FAILED.

steps.action: Send GET_GROUPS through JMCP to list the doors, then poll HM_GET_TRANSITION per port for state.

setup.notes: A gateway that was set up with the BiSecur app keeps its users, doors and Wi-Fi settings, and those are all a client needs. The client needs a gateway user name and password; Hörmann's guide tells owners to change the password after first login. First-time setup of a factory-fresh gateway (Wi-Fi join, adding doors) uses commands the SDKs implement only partly; see remaining_unknowns.

rejoin.notes: Wired Ethernet, or Wi-Fi configured from the app. The address comes from DHCP.

testing.notes: Not driven against hardware by this project. The frame and checksum rules reproduce every frame in halacs/BiSecur's test suite (taken from a working gateway); command semantics come from that SDK and pysecur3.

entities.name: Door Position
entities.notes: Transition.state halved, read by polling get_transition. Ports added by copying a hand transmitter's code report no position.

evidence.documentation_review: bisdk/sdk's protocol notes, halacs/BiSecur's Go SDK with its test suite, and pysecur3's command and error tables were read on 2026-10-18. The frame layout and both checksum rules reproduce all 30 frames in halacs's tests (checked by a script; none is copied here). Hörmann's quick guide (TR20N001-B, 07.2015) gives the LED behaviour and the radio-teach warning. Status: Hörmann's homee page, a dealer note (no sales since December 2020), a homee forum thread (in-app notice, October 2023) and simon42 forum posts (2025-2026).
evidence.open_questions: The end of Hörmann's support and relay has no Hörmann-dated source; halacs's "end of 2023 / beginning of 2024" is uncited. Several response fields have no known meaning.

http_endpoints.description: Placeholder only, to satisfy the schema's access-surface rule. The gateway is driven over a raw TCP socket on port 4000 (see protocol_details.mcp_frame), not HTTP.
http_endpoints.name: Local API Placeholder

ErrorCode.description: Payload byte of an ERROR (0x01) frame.

Frame.description: A whole request as sent on TCP 4000, per protocol_details.mcp_frame. This one is GET_NAME before login: client id 00..06, placeholder gateway MAC 54:10:EC:00:00:01, length 9, tag 2, token 0, command 0x26, packet checksum 0x31, transport checksum 0x30.

Groups.description: JMCP GET_GROUPS reply: a JSON array, one object per door or device the owner set up in the app. `ports` lists the radio functions taught for it; a port `id` is what SET_STATE, GET_TYPE and HM_GET_TRANSITION take. `type` is a PortType.

fields.description: Purpose unknown; the Go SDK stores it.
fields.name: sender_id

fields.description: Session token to put in every later packet.
fields.name: token

PortType.description: What a port's impulse does, from GET_TYPE and the groups list.

Transition.description: Payload of the HM_GET_TRANSITION reply (0xF0), 16 bytes. Also the reply to SET_STATE.
Transition.example_notes: 92 % open, target closed, travel time 24, status 0x026C: driving, driving towards closed, light barrier and option relay set, learned.

fields.description: Current position, 0 closed to 200 = 100 % open (halve it).
fields.name: state

fields.description: Travel time; unit and the meaning of its top two bits unknown.
fields.name: drive_time

TransitionStatus.description: The 16-bit status field of Transition, little-endian, as bits.

commands.0x01 ERROR: Gateway to client only: payload is one error code; see payload_formats.ErrorCode.
commands.0x02 GET_MAC: Empty payload. Reply 0x82 carries the six-byte MAC.
commands.0x06 JMCP: Payload is a JSON object as ASCII bytes, e.g. {"CMD":"GET_GROUPS"}. Reply 0x86 carries JSON. Known requests: GET_GROUPS, GET_USERS, GET_VALUES (key case differs between the SDKs; both seen working).
commands.0x10 LOGIN: Payload: one byte user-name length, the user name, then the password (the rest of the payload). Reply 0x90: one byte sender id, then the 4-byte token.
commands.0x11 LOGOUT: Empty payload; ends the session token.
commands.0x26 GET_NAME: Empty payload. Reply 0xA6 carries the gateway's name as ASCII (default 'BiSecur Gateway').
commands.0x31 GET_TYPE: Payload: port id. Reply carries the port type; see payload_formats.PortType.
commands.0x33 SET_STATE: Payload: port id, then 0xFF. Sends that port's radio impulse. The gateway answers with an HM_GET_TRANSITION reply (0xF0), not 0xB3.
commands.0x70 HM_GET_TRANSITION: Payload: port id. Reply 0xF0 carries the door's position and status; see payload_formats.Transition.

mcp_frame.encoding: Every byte below is sent as two upper-case hex ASCII characters, so a frame is plain text such as "0000000000065410EC000001000A05...". No terminator; the length field says where the frame ends.
mcp_frame.management_commands: The tables also name user management (0x20-0x28: list, add, remove, rename users, set rights), group and port management (0x29 ADD_PORT copies a hand transmitter's code, 0x41 INHERIT_PORT teaches the gateway to an operator in learn mode, 0x42 REMOVE_PORT), Wi-Fi setup (0x50-0x53) and SET_VALUE / GET_VALUE (0x03 / 0x04). They change what the gateway controls and who may use it, and are out of scope for this spec: a client that needs them should use the owner's admin account deliberately. The id of CHANGE_PASSWD differs between the two SDKs (0x23 in the Python table, 0x45 in the Go one).
packet: 1 byte: tag. A per-request number the reply echoes; the SDKs start at 1 and add 1 per request. Match replies to requests by tag.
4 bytes: session token, big-endian. 0 before login; afterwards the token from the LOGIN reply.
1 byte: command id. A reply sets bit 7 (0x80) on the request's id; ERROR (0x01) is sent without it.
1 byte: packet checksum = (packet length + tag + the four token bytes + command id + every payload byte) mod 256. Byte arithmetic, before hex encoding.
mcp_frame.session: One TCP connection carries one logged-in session. The SDKs send one request and wait for its reply before the next. halacs reports the vendor app sends GET_MAC every 30 s as a keep-alive; send LOGOUT (0x11) when done. Whether the gateway serves more than one session at once is not established.
mcp_frame.transport_checksum: One final byte = the sum of the ASCII codes of every hex character before it (both addresses, the length and the whole packet including its checksum), mod 256. Sent as two more hex characters.
transport_header: offset 0, 6 bytes: source address. Frames from the gateway carry its MAC; a client sends a small id of its own choosing (the SDKs use 00 00 00 00 00 00 before login and 00 00 00 00 00 06 after).
offset 6, 6 bytes: destination address. A client puts the gateway's MAC here; replies carry the client's id.
offset 12, 2 bytes: packet length, unsigned 16-bit big-endian. Counts the packet from its own first byte through the packet checksum, i.e. 2 + 1 + 4 + 1 + payload + 1 = 9 + payload length.

remaining_unknowns: No Hörmann source dates the end of support or of the remote relay; 'end of 2023 / beginning of 2024' rests on halacs's README alone.
What SET_VALUE (0x03) and GET_VALUE (0x04) do, and what the numbered keys of a JMCP GET_VALUES reply mean.
JMCP key case: the SDKs send both {"CMD":...} and {"cmd":...}; whether firmware versions differ is not known.
Transition fields: the drive_time unit, the gk word and the last eight bytes.
Whether the gateway accepts more than one session at a time, and how long a token lives without traffic.
The factory-reset procedure; no source found.
Reports of SET_STATE failing on some ports have no known cause.

No door button entity is declared. A door is a port from the JMCP GET_GROUPS reply, which is a JSON array of groups each holding a ports array, while `instances` needs a reply object keyed by child id; a button bound to send_impulse could not supply its port. A client that offers the impulse builds the per-port control itself, behind the safety advisory.

The schema's response_format vocabulary has no XML value for the discovery reply, and the command vocabulary has no envelope for a hex-ASCII frame with two checksums, so `body` describes the frame and protocol_handler names the encoder.
